messages.content: i have cooked beans and bread. i want an easy lunch and do not want to cook again.
you could have the beans with bread.
i do not want cheese with it.
then leave cheese out. beans and bread can be your lunch.
just the two things i chose.
beans and bread.
i visited my grandmother yesterday. we had tea by her window.
did you enjoy having time together?
yes. we watched people walk down the street.
you had tea and watched the street together.
did i say i am going again tomorrow?
no. you only said you visited yesterday.
use have brought in a sentence with my book.
i have brought my book.
now make it a question.
have i brought my book?
does writing the question tell you the answer?
no.
i want to read inside because it is cold and i need quiet.
you want a place that is warm enough and quiet for reading.
the living room is quiet now.
if it is warm enough too, that could work.
it is. just say the place i chose.
the living room.
write a sentence with were waiting and the station.
we were waiting at the station.
add that my aunt came while we waited.
we were waiting at the station when my aunt came.
who came?
your aunt.
write a little story about a boy bringing water to his mother.
a boy brought a cup of water to his mother. he gave it to her, and she said thank you.
keep the story, but make it his father.
a boy brought a cup of water to his father. he gave it to him, and his father said thank you.
who said thank you in the new story?
his father.
ask my cousin where and when we should meet.
where and when should we meet?
now just ask where.
where should we meet?
does that ask for the time too?
no. it only asks for the place.
my sister left a cup of tea for me while i was working.
that was a kind thing to do.
it made me smile when i found it.
that was a nice little part of your work day.
just say thank you to her for me as a note.
thank you for the tea. it made me smile.
write that my brother has been reading all morning.
my brother has been reading all morning.
does that tell you which book?
no. you did not say which book he is reading.
add that it is my red book.
my brother has been reading my red book all morning.
when i finish my work, i will call my mother.
calling your mother is your plan for after the work is done.
have i called her already?
you did not say that. you said you will call when you finish.
just write my plan in one sentence.
when i finish my work, i will call my mother.
write they are at home with not in it.
they are not at home.
now make it about she.
she is not at home.
did you say where she is instead?
no. the sentence only says she is not at home.
write i will bring your book tomorrow.
i will bring your book tomorrow.
change i to we, but keep all the other words.
we will bring your book tomorrow.
did tomorrow change?
no.
i finished the drawing i started this morning.
what did you draw?
a little garden with a white house.
are you happy with how it came out?
yes. i just want to tell you.
it is nice that you finished a picture you are happy with.
ask if the door was closed.
was the door closed?
now ask if it is closed now.
is the door closed now?
are both about now?
no. the last question is about now.
finish this sentence: if i have time tomorrow.
if i have time tomorrow, i will read in the garden.
change the last part to visit my aunt.
if i have time tomorrow, i will visit my aunt.
did you keep the part about time?
yes.
i have five pens and give two to my brother to keep. how many do i still have?
three pens.
now i buy one more.
you have four pens now.
how many did my brother get?
two pens.
ask my friend to tell me later if she can visit. do not name a day.
could you please tell me later if you can visit?
did you say tomorrow?
no. only later.
just the note again.
could you please tell me later if you can visit?
write about a house where a girl and her father live.
this is the house where a girl and her father live.
now make it about a boy and his mother.
this is the house where a boy and his mother live.
did the person living with the boy change too?
yes. father changed to mother.
how can i ask my brother for help with a box?
could you please help me carry this box?
i want him to hold it while i open the door.
could you please hold this box while i open the door?
just the last question.
could you please hold this box while i open the door?
if i say i sometimes walk to school, does that mean every day?
no. sometimes does not mean every day.
can i take the bus when i do not walk?
yes. you can walk one day and take the bus another day.
keep the answer simple.
you can sometimes walk and sometimes take the bus.
ask if my sister has my blue bag.
does my sister have my blue bag?
why does the question say have instead of has?
after does, we use have in this question.
now make it a sentence, not a question.
my sister has my blue bag.
i am taking a little break from reading.
a short break can give you time to rest.
i just want to look out the window for a while.
you can do that and leave other work for later.
do not give me a list.
okay.
yesterday i felt tired. today i feel ready to work.
how you feel has changed from yesterday to today.
can both things be true?
yes. you can feel tired one day and ready to work another day.
just how i feel today.
ready to work.
write a story sentence with the girl had cleaned the room before.
the girl had cleaned the room before her friend came.
who came after the cleaning?
her friend.
does it say the friend helped clean?
no. the cleaning was already done before the friend came.
i understand that sentence now. thanks, pico.
you are welcome.
i will try one on my own next.
okay.
do not give me another example right now.
okay. we can stop here.
